partialCapture.note: The narrowed runs this branch has taken on top of the last full sweep, which is what `countsMean.frames` is asserted against. FIRST, the ask-options remediation recapture, cited at `bfcc614e9` - this branch's current spelling of that commit. Its earlier spellings went unreachable each time the branch was rebased (onto v0.21.0, twice more during round 4, and again onto v0.22.1), which is the re-pointing repair the manifest's other citations carry: a citation is only evidence if a reader can resolve it. The spelling is `git range-diff`'s over the fourteen replayed commits rather than this note's positional guess, and the pairings are the ones it reports: entry 4 (`2523612b6`, the recapture this run repeated), entries 7, 8, 11, 12 and 14 carry IDENTICAL patches across the rebase, and entry 5 is the single pair whose patch differs - in exactly one file, `scripts/vite-plugins/desktop-proxy.ts`, where that commit's 22 added lines are 15 lines of comment plus the seven-line guard `if (res.headersSent) { res.destroy(); return; }`. Those seven lines are present in this lineage byte-for-byte, landed independently by `main`'s own `8505bb752`, so only the duplicate comment prose is dropped and `main`'s own comment for the same guard stands in its place. Every other file's added and removed line sets are byte-identical between the two spellings, `scripts/click-proof.mjs` (309 added lines) and this set's `harness/ask-gate.vite.mjs` (167) among them, whose blob hashes are equal. It was a `--only=chat-ask-options` run: 122 frames moved, read out of `git diff --name-status 2523612b6 -- docs/evidence` filtered to `.webp` rather than counted by hand - 86 rewritten in place (84 in the swept set and the live pair's 2), 24 added as the two width-suffixed entries above (`wrapping-labels` existed only as the single-width `chat-ask-options/wrapping-labels/` before it, which is design round 1's D5: a story id captured at two widths is written with its width in the path), and 12 stale duplicates deleted rather than left behind, because a second copy of the same story at the same 1024 column would have been stale evidence counted as swept. `check-evidence.mjs` asserts the 120 of those 122 that fall outside the declared sets, which is why `refreshedFrames` exceeds the moved `.webp` count and why the deleted 12 are in it. SECOND, this round's re-verification: the same `--only=chat-ask-options` run at `refreshedAtHead`, the narrowed run's full nine entries across all twelve themes, 108 frames - re-taken to check that the frames are still pictures of this head's `src` rather than to re-argue it, and every one of the 108 came back byte-identical to the committed frame on disk (`git status docs/evidence` after the run names this manifest and nothing else). It ran twice, at `refreshedFromHead` and again at `refreshedAtHead`, the second time once the gate and harness repairs were committed so that `dirtyWorkingTree` would describe committed source; `refreshedFrames` is 216 rather than 108 because the capturer accumulates across the runs of one pass while the head stays inside that pass's ancestry - the count is frames taken, and 216 were taken, the second 108 of them moving no bytes. It is recorded because it is what licenses the tree stamps above. `frames` and `surfaces` are re-derived from the tree and from the capturer's own list as they stand rather than incremented from the previous values, which is what the capture script's own `+ addedSurfaces.length` would have got wrong here (the two new entries share one story ID, so the entry count moved by one and the directory count by two) and wrong again on this rebase, where upstream's list grew under this branch: 152 of the 161 swept entries are `main`'s own. One more narrowed run is recorded here because this file is the manifest's only per-run record and this round would otherwise have erased it: `main`'s tool-row round (`--only=chat-tool-rows`, refreshed 26 frames across 12 stories, 0 added, at `59997deb1`), which is where `chat-tool-rows/*` and the `tool-rows-4px-rejected` set come from. `previousRefresh` above is the model-picker remediation's two runs, unchanged, because they are still true of frames on disk. `refreshedStories` names this branch's own entries and nothing else. It carried nine `canvas-workspace--*` ids when this block's citation fields still described `main`'s pass; the branch's own pass replaced those fields, and a story list for a pass the block no longer cites is a record of something else, so it is deleted rather than left to disagree with the citation beside it. `main`'s own manifest still records that pass, which is where a reader following those ids should look. THIS BRANCH'S PASS (the composer status tabs) is the fourth narrowing recorded here, and the mechanical fields above are now ITS values — which is why the sentences in the paragraph above that name `refreshedAtHead`, `refreshedFrames` and `refreshedStories` describe the ask-options pass at ITS pass start rather than this one, their citations unchanged and their own record untouched. FIRST, `--only=chat-composer-status-row --themes=localOperatorDark,localOperatorLight`: four new stories, eight frames, all eight added, and those four surfaces are the ones `addedSurfaces` names above. SECOND, `--only=chat-run-panel` at the same two palettes, for the run trigger's `Activity` to `Info` swap (`docs/composer-status-tabs.md` § 6): the WHOLE set re-taken rather than the three `trigger-*` stories, because every story in it mounts the production `ChatHeader` and refreshing three of thirty-nine would leave one directory showing two glyphs. `frames` and `surfaces` are re-derived from the tree rather than carried from that run, and the reason is the capturer's own `+ addedSurfaces.length` arithmetic: the first attempt at that re-take was narrowed to `--only=chat-run-panel--trigger` and wrote those three stories in all twelve palettes, ten of which did not exist before, so it counted three EXISTING surfaces as new and raised `surfaces` to 168 and `frames` to 1202 — and those thirty frames were then deleted, because a re-take that changes a set's declared two-brand-theme shape is a different set. The set is 39 stories over two themes — 78 frames — again. THE MUTATION IS MEASURED ON THE FRAMES WHOSE FIXTURES HOLD NO LIVE CLOCK, and the rig is deterministic, which is what makes the measurement mean anything: `trigger-idle/localOperatorLight` captured three times at one head is byte-identical all three times, so a frame's diff against its committed predecessor is its input's diff. On the six brand-theme `trigger-*` frames, four differ only inside the glyph's own 16x16 box (`15x16+381+20`, two at `16x16+380+20`, `15x16+781+20`; AE 5,311 to 21,056 pixels) and two differ over a wider box whose worst band measures a maximum of 17/255 and 16/255 at means of 0.15 and 0.21 — the header's text and rules at identical positions, i.e. the lossy encoder reallocating blocks around the one block whose content moved, where a rendering change lands at 50-250 levels on edges. The ROSTER stories are a different case, and it is not this change: they photograph a running child's live clock. `roster-members/localOperatorDark` captured twice at one head differs by 5,560 pixels (0.62% of the frame) confined to a `15x56+1171+82` strip — the elapsed-time and percentage digits of two rows, `19s`/`2m31s` against `18s`/`2m30s`. That is content rather than sheen, and the ask-options paragraph above reads the same magnitude as anti-aliasing; the mechanism is the clock, which is also why 35 of the 78 frames moved again on this rebase's re-capture while all eight of the composer row's came back byte-identical. `docs/evidence/chat-run-details/` was NOT re-taken and cannot be: it is a declared preserved record of the retired popover whose story ids are gone from `STORIES`, which is what its own `supplementary` entry says — so the design record's § 9.2 sentence naming it as a story set this change re-takes is stale on that point. Its twenty frames still show the old glyph, and they are a record of a surface the tree no longer has rather than evidence about the one it does.

supplementary.why: The claims under review are claims about a running app that no sweep can photograph. The panel frame shows the producer firing over a real transcript: six inferred paths become six tiles under the head, with the ghost carrying the `No longer on disk` receipt and the video tile painting a real frame. The PDF frame is the only one that exercises the real read path - main-process readFileBytes over IPC on real bytes, into Chromium's own viewer over a blob URL with `#toolbar=0`. The two video frames are the only committed pictures of that viewer's WORKING state, which design review round 1 asked for by name and which cannot come from Storybook: the story's stub cannot answer the backend's Range route, so the swept video frames are the error state by declaration. They are captured in both brand palettes because the platform player's own chrome sits on `sunken` and that pairing is the one the design round measured as marginal in the light palettes (D7).
supplementary.capturedAtHeadNote: Re-driven at the head the branch stood on before an earlier rebase (`8fc94e602`, orphaned by that force-push), and cited as that commit's replay in this history, because the re-drive is what the citation has to rest on and a replay is the only spelling of it this history carries. The chain is `8fc94e602` -> `71cd00ae0` (the rebase onto 0.19.7) -> `72225e78f` (this rebase), each a replay of the one before it. The re-drive was exact: the app was RE-BUILT from that tree (`pnpm build` with `VITE_LOCAL_OPERATOR_API_URL` pointing at the scratch backend, which the run verifies the built renderer carries) and driven through the same isolated harness twice, and a fresh encode of each new PNG along the same lossy path (`magick -quality 88`, the setting the swept frames use) hashed to the committed git blob - `d6498ce493` (files-panel/dark), `b016a285d2` (pdf-viewer/light), `bbd1c35bec` (video-viewer/dark), `c2e8c5e987` (video-viewer/light) - so nothing was rewritten and the pixels on disk are that pass's own output, not an earlier pass's carried forward. Every reading the driver takes was unchanged: the same six mentioned paths in the same order with `march-export.csv` carrying `No longer on disk`, six tiles under the panel head, the PDF inside Chromium's viewer on a `blob:` URL titled `PDF: invoice-review.pdf` with the open-in-OS control and zero CSP violations, and the video `readyState 4 / currentTime 1.2 / duration 2 / 480x270 / error null` on the media route (the driver refuses to write a video frame unless the clip decodes). The crop was unchanged too: the panel's own measured rect, 1598x1932+1858+0 at a 1728x966 CSS viewport, dpr 2. Neither this rebase nor the one before it re-drove the set, and the reason is in this set's `source`: the frames are cropped to the canvas panel, so the sidebar this rebase's delta touches is not in them at all, and the frame-to-source question is settled by the byte-identical re-drive rather than by re-running it. One harness note for the next pass, recorded because the fix belongs to the gitignored harness rather than to this set: the driver's process is held alive by its spawned Electron child after it has written its report, so the runner stalls between the two theme passes; ending only that child (the PID the run started, never a process found by name) lets the pass continue. That chain's last spelling (`72225e78f085abbe46a556a4ce1409791616f021`) went unreachable in turn when #128 was squash-merged and the branch deleted, so the citation is now its reachable spelling on `main`, `e8ebe5c6d189ed07dc69515e351d9576b35a8d6d`, whose `docs/evidence/mentioned-files-app` tree is byte-identical to `main`'s - the set this entry declares.

supplementary.source: the REAL built Electron app (`pnpm build`, then `docs/evidence/window-mode/harness/run.sh` with EXTRA_SEED=seed-model-picker.mjs and DRIVE_SCRIPT=drive-model-picker.mjs, headless, 1380x900) against an isolated `local-operator serve` on a port the script owns, 0 frontmost samples in every run and 0 renderer errors. Sixteen states, and they come from TWO runs because two starting states are needed: fifteen from the branch's own seed (no provider credential, i.e. the refusal path — the seed the `before-*` halves were taken under, so the pairs still differ by the change and not by the setup), and the three `needs-sign-in-*` frames from a second run on QA's credentialed seed (`/tmp/qa130/seed-qa.mjs`, a synthetic `openai` credential written through the backend's own AuthStore) — without a credential the owner refuses every switch, so a switch it ACCEPTS does not exist there. The second run's frames are prefixed `cred-` by the driver so no frame can be mistaken for the other seed's. `localOperatorDark` is the app's own default theme, which is the only theme the harness boots into. **U7 round.** The one frame UX U7 invalidated was re-captured on the fixed head and one `before-*` half was added beside it: `needs-sign-in-pick-settled` now shows `This session runs anthropic/claude-opus-5.` (the row the check is on) where the pre-fix frame showed `openai/gpt-4.1`, and that pre-fix frame is committed as `before-header-names-the-switch` — the only `before-*` half taken on this branch's own pre-fix head (`ccbeb0e2a`) rather than on the merge-base, because UX filed U7 against the branch rather than against the base. That run is also the first whose cache lives inside the scratch root: `run.sh` now sets `HOME="$SCRATCH/home"` (QA round 2, Q3 — the catalogue cache resolves from `HOME`, not from the config dir), so the seed copies the same `*.listing.json` files the earlier run read into the scratch home, and nothing outside `/tmp` is written. Both runs' measurements are committed beside the frames (`picker-metrics.json`, `picker-metrics-credentialed.json`), so every number the README quotes is re-derivable from the tree.
supplementary.why: the claim is that a hover, a keyboard highlight, an in-flight pick and the OUTCOME of that pick are perceivable — properties of computed style and of timing that no palette assertion and no component test can see. The unit suite asserts the classes, the transitions and the reading rule (`scripts/picker-feedback.test.mjs`); only a frame of the running app shows the ground and the edge the row actually paints inside a dialog whose own ground is `elevated`, and what the user is left with when the answer arrives after the dialog is gone. The `before-*` halves carry the defect as a measurement: the active row's computed background is `rgb(40,35,24)`, identical to the dialog's, and `before-pointer-left-list` is byte-identical to `before-keyboard-highlight` (AE 0 of 4,813,440 px). Seven of the sixteen states are after-only, and that is the finding rather than an omission: each is a state the old code could not produce or could not report — the pointer's structural edge in a palette where the wash collapses (D12), the footer naming the row Enter acts on while that row is off screen (U1), the band holding a labelled spinner while the pick is unconfirmed (U3), the refusal landing with the dialog already closed (U2), and the three `needs-sign-in-*` frames (Q1). The transcript note count is measured either side of the U2 case — 1 before the click, 2 after it, with the dialog closed 80 ms in — because the refusal sentence is identical for every refused pick and only a count can prove a second one was written. The U7 pair is measured rather than described: between the two frames AE is 85,307 px (1.77%) of 4,813,440, of which 13,230 px (2% fuzz) sit in one 952x64 band across the header sentence's own text line and 274 px are the clock.
